themes_detail.label: Street Light Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street light outages have spiked dramatically to 27 complaints THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 5.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 360% increase (z-score: 7.42)—signaling a potential infrastructure failure affecting public safety and visibility across Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights.
evidence: 27 Street Light Condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (360% spike)
Z-score of 7.42 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Community Board has repeatedly requested DOT capital funding for transit/infrastructure upgrades, suggesting systemic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Contact DOT to determine root cause: equipment failure, maintenance backlog, or supply chain issue specific to CD109
Interview residents and safety advocates about impact on evening commutes, personal safety, and street-level commerce

themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints have surged to 3 cases THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—potentially indicating a contamination event or food safety violation in a local restaurant or food establishment.
evidence: 3 Food Poisoning complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% spike)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Timing coincides with week when Street Light and Street Light Condition issues also peak, suggesting possible recent event or change
reporting_angles: Obtain 311 complaint details to identify specific restaurant(s) or food vendor(s) involved
Cross-reference with NYC Department of Health inspection records and violations for establishments in the district
Interview affected residents about symptoms, timing, and food source to establish possible venue connection

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints peaked at 10 cases 3 WEEKS AGO compared to a baseline of 1.4 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 627% spike (z-score: 5.77)—indicating a growing homelessness or rough-sleeping crisis in visible public spaces throughout the district.
evidence: 10 Encampment complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (627% spike)
Z-score of 5.77 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Community Board has standing budget request for outreach services to vulnerable populations and public health programs, suggesting known need
reporting_angles: Map encampment locations (subway stations, parks, commercial corridors) and interview residents/business owners about safety concerns
Report on response from NYPD, Sanitation, and homeless outreach services; assess adequacy of city resources
Profile individuals experiencing homelessness to understand housing loss triggers (e.g., evictions, economic displacement linked to Columbia University expansion)

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Spike
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 9 cases LAST WEEK compared to a baseline of 2.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 324% increase (z-score: 6.53)—suggesting either inadequate waste collection capacity, illegal dumping, or rodent/pest activity linked to accumulated refuse.
evidence: 9 Residential Disposal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (324% spike)
Z-score of 6.53 indicates statistically extreme deviation
Correlates with broader sanitation concerns: 719 Unsanitary Condition complaints over 90-day period (top 5 overall)
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to determine if collection frequency was reduced or delays occurred in the district
Photograph affected blocks and interview residents about whether refuse is piling up on curbs or in building hallways
Investigate possible connection to rat sightings or pest complaints; cross-check with Unsanitary Condition reports

themes_detail.label: Building Inspection Surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints spiked to 4 cases 2 WEEKS AGO compared to a baseline of 0.5 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% spike (z-score: 7.0)—indicating a concentrated code enforcement action or targeted building violations investigation in the district.
evidence: 4 SPIT complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (700% spike)
Z-score of 7.0 indicates statistically extreme deviation
374 building alteration permits filed in last 90 days; 332 are alteration type, suggesting active renovation/rehab activity
reporting_angles: Determine which building(s) triggered SPIT inspections and what violations were cited
Review DOB permits and violations to assess whether enforcement is targeting illegal conversions, overcrowding, or habitability issues
Connect to Hill Top Apartments ULURP application (1727 Amsterdam Avenue) currently in public review—does enforcement signal broader affordability or displacement concerns?
